correctness.rationale: The complete language, automaton and enumerator are correct under the frozen assumptions. A k-clique in any orientation either contains a directed cycle (read arbitrary signs by walking forward/backward around it) or is a transitive tournament. This gives the lower language inclusion. Orienting edges increasingly in a proper k-colouring gives a signed-walk map to the transitive tournament and the upper inclusion. A length-k monochromatic run is impossible there by strict rank changes; each shorter run can go from one extreme rank to the other in its prescribed number of steps, and alternating runs concatenate. The complete DFA has a start, two sets of k-1 run counters and a dead state. Every state is reachable; a same-sign continuation that just fills a forbidden run distinguishes different run counters and separates each from the start and opposite counters; the empty continuation distinguishes the dead state. This works also for k=1, with start and dead states only. The two choices of starting sign and the compositions into allowable run lengths yield the displayed generating function. The independent bounded replay in /workspace/branches/ba5b573b-c697-4755-b510-70c88a0b7b9e/replay.py checked every orientation of six small graphs on words through length 7, DFA comparisons through length 9 and state/enumerator checks for k=1 through 5. The C5 witness reached {1,3,4}, {3}, {2,4}, {1,3}, then the empty set, as claimed. All supporting files including the supplied checker and its output were inspected; the uploaded checker was not executed. Bounded checks corroborate, not replace, the argument.
